routes.description: Source-to-ledger coverage. The existing review endpoints select invoices by creation date; this one selects every source family by its own activity date, so a receipt taken today against an old invoice cannot fall outside the review window.
Accrue bed-day charges on demand. Active admissions return an estimate only. After discharge the saved occupancy evidence is staged and billed with idempotent night identities.
Vitals history for one admission, with abnormality flags derived from adult reference ranges.
Record ward vitals against an admission. Separate from POST /api/observations so that ward care does not depend on the OPD module being enabled for the facility.
Public facility administrator invitation endpoints. These must be accessible before the invited user logs in.
Public authentication endpoints
Logout requires the current authentication session.
Session validation requires a valid session.
Public staff invitation endpoints. Keep these public so invited staff can validate and accept their link.
Bed set-up. Beds are created in a batch because a ward is set up in one sitting: a prefix, a first number and a count, or an explicit list of numbers.
Release a cleaned bed back into service (Cleaning -> Available). Without this, every discharge permanently removes a bed from the usable board because nothing else restores 'Available'.

Change a bed's housekeeping status. 'Occupied' is rejected by the query layer: occupancy must come from an admission. A bed holding a patient cannot be changed until that patient is discharged or transferred.
Manual accounting record only; no bank, card or mobile transfer is initiated.
POST keeps search terms out of URLs, reverse-proxy access logs and browser history.

Billing a session is a finance action, not a clinical one: the ward clerk who recorded the session should not also decide what it costs. It therefore needs the billing permission rather than the dialysis recording permission.

Impairment and revaluation are accounting judgements that move money between the register and the ledger, so they are gated with `assets.dispose` — the write-off authority — not with register-edit rights.
Mappings are facility-specific clinician reviews, never automatic conversions.

The reference schedule, straight from the module that computes against it. The screen reads its antigen list from here rather than carrying a second copy that would drift the first time a dose is added.
Ward board: occupancy, per-admission vitals status and note counts. One scoped call so the ward screen and dashboard do not fan out.

Dispatch review queue. A lost provider response leaves a durable reservation that blocks every later action on the claim. These routes are the only sanctioned way to look at and resolve it. They never call a payer and never re-dispatch.

Receive stock into a batch. Tops up an existing batch number instead of failing, so a second delivery of the same lot is not rejected by the unique index.
Batches with their expiry status, ordered earliest expiry first. Everything reaches the facility through inventory_items, because inventory_batches has no facility column of its own.
Expired and near-expiry stock for the facility.
Close only the retry identity, never a recorded receipt or its stock.
A status lookup never turns NOT_FOUND into permission to use a new identity.
Full invoice: header, line items with their clinical provenance and every payment already recorded.

Finalized statements contain diagnosis information, so billing and clinical read permission are both required. The service commits an access log before returning the statement. No provider request settles an invoice here.
Void an invoice. Audit-preserving: the row and its lines remain, marked voided, so the record is never destroyed.
Shift handover: notes for a day grouped by shift. Defaults to today; pass ?date=YYYY-MM-DD&shift=Morning to narrow.

Record ward or clinic vitals. Inpatient vitals are recorded against an admission, which guarantees the patient is actually in a bed at this facility. A bare patient payload is no longer accepted: observations carry no facility column, so un
Ask before prescribing. Read-only. It records nothing, so a prescriber can check a name without leaving a trace of a decision they have not made.
Search data stays in the request body rather than a URL. Each bounded page is facility-scoped and access entries must be durable before it is returned.
Super-admin pages are metadata/provisioning only, never facility finance.

POST /api/platform/facilities Create a facility and its initial onboarding record atomically.
PATCH /api/platform/facilities/:id Update facility configuration without permitting tenant reassignment.
GET /api/platform/facilities/:id/onboarding Retrieve the existing onboarding record for a facility.
POST /api/platform/facilities/:id/onboarding Create onboarding only when no record exists.
GET /api/platform/facility-admin-invitations List invitation metadata without exposing token hashes.
POST /api/platform/facility-admin-invitations Create a secure invitation for a facility administrator (Platform Super Admin only).
POST /api/platform/facility-admin-invitations/:id/reissue Replace the old token and extend the invitation by 48 hours.
POST /api/platform/facility-admin-invitations/:id/revoke Revoke an invitation that has not already been accepted or revoked.
POST /api/platform/rbac/catalogue/apply Create the catalogue roles this tenant does not have yet (additive only).
GET /api/platform/rbac/roles Return real database roles, their current permission assignments, and the permission catalogue.
PUT /api/platform/rbac/roles/:id/permissions Save a facility-specific permission override without changing shared defaults.
POST /api/platform/tenants Create a tenant and provision its tenant-scoped FACILITY_ADMIN and staff roles.
PATCH /api/platform/tenants/:id Update tenant configuration.
A staff member viewing a patient's card SVG is an auditable read.

Resolve a scanned card. Scanning is a lookup under the staff member's own session — it is not an authentication event. The response says so, so nobody mistakes a successful scan for "the patient is verified".

Re-issue a manual link. Returns a *new* token: the previous slip stops working the moment this succeeds. That is the correct behaviour for a lost card, and it is also why the raw token is never stored for display.

Activate an account. The token arrives in the request **body**, never the URL. The browser reads it from the URL fragment (which servers never see) and posts it here, so it does not land in an access log or a Referer header.

Download. Generated on the fly and streamed with `Content-Disposition: attachment`. There is no stored file and no public URL, so a link forwarded to the wrong person resolves to 401 unless they also hold a live portal session.
Search terms are sent in the authenticated body, not a URL that proxies may log.

The landing page's headline figures. They are aggregates, so there is no patient identity to log; each figure applies its own permission and module gate and reports why it is missing rather than returning a zero.

Manual verification. For regulators without an authorised API, and for any case where the automated check cannot decide. The source and date are recorded, and the result is never labelled as automated.
Regulator catalogue for the invitation popup. Read-only and static; it tells the client which regulators exist, which staff roles they cover, and which of them can be checked automatically.

Pre-invitation check. Runs the registry lookup and stores the result, returning a `credentialId` that the invitation endpoint will require for a clinical role. A simulated answer is returned as simulated and is not invitable.
Replace the assignable roles on one staff account.
Activate or deactivate one staff account.
The tasks one staff role may perform, beside the tasks this facility is allowed to grant it.
Replace the task list of one staff role.

The old free-text path had neither patient scope nor conflict protection. Keep validation and the URL, but refuse all writes instead of silently migrating legacy or signed records into an unaudited workflow.
